subject: AI & Agents
title: Training Data: Garbage In, Garbage Out
description: A short lesson to help you apply Training Data: Garbage In, Garbage Out.

hook.text: An LLM trained on Reddit sounds different from one trained on textbooks. The data defines the model.

buildup.text: Training data includes books, web pages, code, conversations, and academic papers.

discovery.text: Data quality matters more than quantity. Curated data outperforms raw web scrapes.

twist.text: Copyright lawsuits loom. Authors and publishers argue their work was used without permission.

climax.text: The next frontier is synthetic data — AI generating training data for other AI.

punchline.text: You are what you eat. So is AI.

quiz.question: Why is training data quality important for LLMs?
options: Better data quality produces better model outputs
More data always means better results
Data quality doesn't affect the model

details.summary: The quality of training data determines the quality of AI outputs. Biased, inaccurate, or toxic data produces biased, inaccurate, or toxic models. Data curation is among the most important steps in building responsible AI.
details.whyItMatters: Every flaw in AI can be traced back to training data. Understanding this relationship explains why AI exhibits biases, makes errors, and why data quality investment is critical for trustworthy systems.
takeaways: Training data quality directly determines model output quality
Biased data produces biased models — the effect is inescapable
Data curation and filtering are critical for responsible AI

faq.question: What makes training data high quality?
faq.answer: Diverse representation of topics and perspectives, factual accuracy, minimal toxic content, and proper deduplication. High-quality data is carefully filtered, which is expensive and time-consuming but essential.

faq.question: Can bad training data be fixed after the model is trained?
faq.answer: Partially, through fine-tuning and RLHF. But fundamental biases from pre-training are difficult to fully remove. Prevention through data curation is far more effective than post-hoc correction.
